title: Introduce stage-aware presubmit snapshots and quiet-merge mode
author: Amina Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight presubmit snapshotter (opt-in) and a quiet-merge mode for release windows; no API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: We have recurring noisy presubmit runs that make it hard to reason about regressions during staged releases. Teams have asked for a lower-cost presubmit option that produces reproducible artifact snapshots for fast triage, plus a merge mode that reduces churn during release quiet windows. This PR introduces a stage-aware presubmit snapshotter and a quiet-merge mode that defers non-essential CI shards in release windows.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a presubmit snapshot step that captures deterministic toolchain manifests, lockfile hashes, and a minimal set of test seeds so infra can reproduce failures without running full integration shards. Snapshots are stored as short-lived build artifacts and indexed by commit and stage.
- Introduces "quiet-merge" pipeline semantics: when a release window label is present, non-blocking/slow CI lanes are soft-snoozed and results annotated on the merge commit rather than gating the merge.
- Implements a lightweight lint runner wrapper (node -> Go shim) to reduce cold-starts and memory footprint for small PRs.
- Adds telemetry hooks that tag presubmit snapshots with stage (dev/canary/release) and sample rates, enabling stage-aware dependency telemetry and aggregated presubmit cost metrics.

Commit summary: 5 commits (squash target)
- Add presubmit snapshotter service and CLI wrapper
- Integrate snapshot publish step into presubmit composite action
- Implement quiet-merge detection and pipeline router change
- Replace node lint entrypoint with go shim for fastpath linting
- Tests, docs, and changelog for CI behavior

Files changed (high level):
- .github/actions/presubmit-snapshot/* (new) — CLI, action.yml, publisher
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml (modified) — stage routing, snapshot step insertion
- .github/workflows/release-window.yaml (modified) — quiet-merge annotations
- infra/ci/router.go (modified) — stage detection and lane throttling
- tools/lint/entrypoint.go (new) — lightweight lint wrapper
- docs/ci/presubmits.md (modified) — usage and opt-in guidance
- test/ci/snapshotter_test.go (new) — unit tests for snapshot behavior

Testing and CI: All CI lanes pass on the final branch. Initial run showed a flaky integration collector test (test/ci/collector_test.go) which was fixed by reducing parallelism and adding a small sleep in the fixture; re-ran twice. Lint and go vet pass. Nightly longtests unaffected because quiet-merge only applies during labeled windows.

Review feedback and threads (summary):
- Diego: requested stronger guarantees on snapshot determinism; asked for explicit lockfile stamps and a note about ephemeral artifact TTL (accepted).
- Jian: asked to gate quiet-merge to only apply when repo-level release window flag is set; implemented an opt-in repo setting and added docs.
- Priya: asked to keep non-blocking lanes observable; added a new dashboard tile and exported a presubmit-snapshot metric.
- Author replies: clarified snapshot contents and added a small CLI mode to allow local reproduction (presubmit-snapshot --replay).

Backward compatibility and opt-in behavior: The snapshotter is opt-in per-team (presubmit config key). Quiet-merge must be explicitly enabled via repo settings or PR label (release/quiet-merge). Default behavior is unchanged. No public API changes.

Performance and cost implications: Early internal trials reduced total presubmit CPU time by ~28% for small PRs (<10 files changed) by diverting heavy lanes into snapshot-only flows. Snapshot artifacts are small (~300KB) and TTL is 6 hours by default to limit storage costs.

Operational notes and rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature-flag gate (ci.feature.presubmit_snapshot = false).
2) Enable for a small team (platform infra) for 1 week and monitor presubmit-cost and false-negative rates.
3) Gradually opt in additional teams while adjusting sample rates.
4) After 4 weeks, consider enabling quiet-merge for scheduled release windows.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals (Diego, Jian, Priya). Created a follow-up Linear to track dashboard polish and sampling rate tuning.

Related work and references: Linear ENG-1421 (presubmit cost profiling), ENG-1488 (release window process improvements), SUP-431 (customer incident where CI flakiness delayed a release).

Notes for reviewers/maintainers: Snapshot artifacts should not be used for long-term forensic needs; they are intended for quick repro and triage. If you need persistent recording, request a longer TTL via infra support.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added for snapshotter core [x] Integration test for pipeline router [x] Docs updated [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan [x] Telemetry exported

If there are concerns about silencing too much during quiet windows we can relax the quiet-merge criteria to only deflect known-expensive lanes rather than all non-blocking lanes.
notes: Opt-in presubmit snapshotter + quiet merge; follow-up tasks created for telemetry dashboard and sample tuning.
